findings.title: Video booking references now lose their credential ID
findings.body: `credentialId` is now set to `undefined` for every non-calendar result. Video results do not satisfy `isCalendarType`, whereas the previous code persisted `result.credentialId` for them. As a result, newly created video references have no credential association; for example, `handleCancelBooking` only calls `deleteMeeting` when the video reference has a `credentialId`, so cancelling these bookings leaves the video meeting active.

findings.title: A secondary collective host calendar is discarded when the primary host has none
findings.body: For a collective booking, destination calendars for secondary hosts are collected, but the initial value is `null` when neither the event type nor the primary organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op. Thus, if only a non-primary collective host has a connected destination calendar, no destination is passed to `EventManager` and that host never receives a calendar event. Initialize this as an empty array before appending host calendars.

findings.title: Creation does not route non-Google integrations to the destination being iterated
findings.body: `createEvent` accepts `externalId` and later records it in the booking reference, but the actual calendar-service call receives only the full event array and a credential ID; `externalId` is never used to select the target. This happens once per destination in `EventManager`. Google was updated to match the credential ID, but Office365, Lark, and the base CalDAV service all select `destinationCalendar[0]` instead. For a collective event with different host calendars, later iterations therefore attempt to create using another host's credential against the first host's calendar (or create duplicates there), while the reference claims the event was created in the later calendar. The selected destination must be forwarded or the event must be narrowed per call, and all calendar services must select it consistently.

findings.title: Only the first collective destination is retained for deferred event creation
findings.body: The new multi-host destination list is reduced to `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` when the booking is persisted. This loses every other host calendar before a pending or paid booking is scheduled. The confirmation and payment handlers rebuild their `CalendarEvent` only from `booking.destinationCalendar` (or the organizer fallback), so confirming a collective booking or completing payment later creates an event only for the first host. Persist enough destination information or rebuild all collective host destinations in those deferred flows.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference
findings.body: In the recurring/all-remaining path, each updated booking's calendar reference is obtained with `.find(...)`, so only its first calendar event is considered. The code then tries that one reference with every credential belonging to the booking owner, rather than using the credential attached to each reference. With multiple collective-host references, secondary host events are never deleted, and the first event is redundantly deleted once per reference (often using credentials that cannot access it). Iterate every updated booking reference and resolve/delete it with that reference's credential.

findings.title: Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar now throw instead of falling back
findings.body: Destructuring an empty/null destination array makes `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, but the Google Meet fallback immediately reads `.integration` from it. A booking that selects Google Meet without a connected destination calendar—precisely the case this fallback is meant to handle—now throws a runtime TypeError instead of switching to Cal Video. Use optional chaining or explicitly handle an absent first destination.

findings.title: Organization creation drops the requested slug when team billing is disabled
findings.body: The condition was reversed: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, the organization now stores neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug`. The supplied slug is still collision-checked and may be registered with Vercel, but it is discarded from the created organization, leaving no persisted identifier for the requested organization URL/domain. The non-team-billing branch needs to retain the slug as before.

findings.title: No regression test covers multiple collective destination calendars
findings.body: The only changed end-to-end assertion adjusts a webhook payload shape; it does not create a collective event with two hosts, distinct credentials, and distinct destination calendars. There is also no coverage for confirmation/payment-delayed creation or recurring cancellation. Such tests are needed to verify that one reference and one event are created, updated, and deleted for each host calendar.
